correctness.rationale: The original defining supremum for FBL^(2)[ℓ₂^n] is identical to π₂ of the incidence operator: admissibility is ∑u_tu_tᵀ⪯I. Three mutually orthogonal projectors have cross-edge block energies (a−1)/a, (b−1)/b and 1/a+1/b. The chosen weights satisfy equality in the weighted-Cauchy upper bound and yield the sharp trace value S². The exact average-edge covariance identity is expanded blockwise, and the explicitly constructed ab test vectors have covariance P_A+P_B+P_C⪯I and all edge norms S/√(ab). Boundary a=1 or b=1 is handled by omitting zero-rank blocks. Analytical proof covers every pair of positive integers; finite checks are only diagnostics.

value.rationale: The 2-summing norm of the complete-bipartite discrete gradient is a canonical Banach-operator invariant of graph incidence maps, not an arbitrary parameter slice. Determining it in closed form for all part sizes, its exact imbalance dependence, and a dimension-sensitive norm-attaining frame answers a motivated natural question previously given only by a variational definition. Nontrivial two-block decomposition and sharp witnesses go beyond substitution in a known norm bound; finite-dimensionality does not diminish an exact all-size classification.
